name: Palladian Construction Crestline Hauler-Rig
description: The Crestline Hauler-Rig is a heavy-duty exo-assisted ground vehicle built around a modular cargo spine and six independently articulated drive wheels, each capable of torque-vectoring across uneven terrain. Its onboard load-balancing AI — called the Ballast Cognition Module — continuously redistributes weight across the chassis to prevent tipping on collapsed infrastructure, rubble fields, and the deeply rutted access roads that connect GLMZ's outer districts to its central arcology cores. Power is drawn from a dual-cell hydrogen compression stack buried beneath the operator cab, giving the Crestline a range of approximately 900 kilometers before refuel under full load.
tactical_use: While not designed for combat, the Crestline is frequently commandeered or hired for high-value smuggling runs through the outer districts, where corporate checkpoints are sparse and road conditions deter pursuit vehicles. Its sheer mass makes it effective as a ramming deterrent. Runners have been known to convert the cargo spine into mobile command posts, weapons caches, or even temporary safe houses during extended operations. The Ballast Cognition Module can be overridden and reprogrammed to accept non-standard cargo configurations — a modification that gray-market mechanics charge premium rates to perform.
cultural_context: The Crestline is the unglamorous backbone of GLMZ's outer-district economy. To the laboring class, it represents reliable work — hauling reclaimed materials, food shipments from Ironclad Agrisystems substations, and prefab housing components. To fixers and logistics-minded operators, it is a slow but dependable asset. There is a working-class pride attached to the Crestline; outer-district drivers often personalize their rigs heavily with painted sigils, district colors, and religious iconography, transforming these industrial machines into rolling cultural statements.
story_hooks: A Crestline carrying a sealed Palladian cargo container has gone missing somewhere in the eastern rubble corridor — the manifest lists building materials, but the weight discrepancy suggests something else entirely.
A driver's Ballast Cognition Module has started routing the vehicle away from its programmed destinations, seemingly of its own volition, always toward the same coordinates in the outer sprawl.

A crew needs to move a large, fragile, and very illegal piece of hardware across three district checkpoints — the only viable option is a Crestline, but the licensed driver refuses to cooperate without leverage.
Two outer-district hauler gangs have gone to war over exclusive Palladian contracts, and a shipment of weapons hidden inside a Crestline's cargo spine is the prize both sides are hunting.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist hexapod hauler with a pronounced angular cab mounted forward-left of a long, modular spine chassis. Six independently articulated wheels with deep treading protrude asymmetrically from reinforced mounting arms. The chassis tapers rearward, terminating in a standardized cargo interface plate. Overall silhouette suggests a mechanical insect adapted for industrial salvage work.
physical_description.dimensions: 14.2 meters long, approximately 3.8 meters wide at wheel track, 2.9 meters to cab roof
physical_description.weight_description: Heavy vehicle requiring dedicated parking infrastructure; fully laden (38,000 kg payload + dry weight ~16,000 kg) demands reinforced loading zones
physical_description.primary_material: Welded steel frame with composite reinforcement panels; cast aluminum wheel hubs
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte coating with visible weld seams; weather-worn patina on working units showing rust bloom and abrasion marks from site work
physical_description.color_scheme: Palladian corporate slate gray base with high-visibility safety striping (reflective white/orange) on wheel wells and cab edges; hydraulic fluid stains and rust streaks typical on operational vehicles
physical_description.interface_elements: Cab features wraparound forward viewports with polarizing smart-glass; side-mounted status displays showing load distribution, fuel state, and AI module activity; manual steering wheel with integrated haptic feedback; roof-mounted beacon (amber/red toggle); exterior pressure-point indicators for load sensors
distinctive_features: Ballast Cognition Module indicator lights (blue LEDs) cycling along chassis spine to show active weight redistribution zones
Six independent wheel modules with visible articulation joints, each capable of ±45° rotation
Hydrogen stack access panels marked with caution chevrons, recessed into undercarriage with exposed thermal dissipation vanes
Modular cargo spine with standardized hardpoint receptacles spaced every 1.2 meters
Operator cab slightly elevated above chassis centerline for terrain visibility despite full load
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Large PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION logo (stylized P in geometric sans-serif) embossed on cab side; construction-grade regulatory stamps (GLMZ Autonomous Load Certification, Hydrogen Safety Class 3); vehicle ID plate mounted below driver viewport
physical_description.condition_typical: Working units show compacted soil in wheel tread, minor dents on cargo interface from repeated coupling cycles, and faint hydraulic seepage patterns around joint articulations. High-hour units exhibit chrome wear on actuator arms and discolored thermal vanes from repeated hydrogen stack cycling.
